recipes.name: Grilled Italian Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat, and lightly oil the grate.

Sprinkle pork chops with salt and black pepper, and grill until the chops are browned, show good grill marks, and are no longer pink in the middle, 5 to 8 minutes per side. An instant-read meat thermometer inserted into the center of a chop should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

Place ham, tomato, and mozzarella cheese slices on each pork chop, and sprinkle with oregano and paprika; cook until the cheese has melted, about 2 more minutes. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Italian Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Grilled pork chops get an Italian-style topping of ham, fresh tomato, and mozzarella cheese slices for a dinner that's ready in just 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: So good my husband couldn't get off the foot of the stairs because he was so full. I did make some minor alterations. First, I grilled the ham and tomatoes. Then, I layered the pork chops with mozzarella cheese, slice of ham, shredded gouda, grilled tomatoes, then garnished with a mixture of salt, pepper, chopped oregano, and chopped parsley. Excellent and well worth every bite! Served with Grilled Green Bean Bundles and Southern as You Can Get Collard Greens.

made this today exactly as described. Both my husband and i really liked the recipe. my chops were about 1/2" thick. I sliced a good quality ham thinly. Used fresh mozzarella and firm fresh tomato. I think in the future, I would place the ham, mozzarella and tomato on the chop for last 3 minutes of cooking.the chops instead of an additional 2 minutes of cooking. I found that I lost grill heat from having to place the ham, mozzarella and tomatoes, it didn't have enough time to warm up. I didn't want to add additional cooking time and risk drying out the chop. Also, I would assemble the ham, mozzarella and tomatoes before opening the grill; then just pop the assembly onto the chop. very good recipe though. will definitely make this again.

I turned this recipe into stuffed Italian pork chops. I started with three-quarter inch butterflied chops that I had intended to stuff and bake but decided to use this recipe instead. I took oversized, deli slices of ham that were on the thick side, topped those with grated mozzarella cheese, oregano and basil. Then I rolled the cheese inside the ham like a burrito. Then put the stuffed ham rolls inside the butterflied chops, sealed them with tooth picks and grilled them as per the directions. In the end, I put a little more mozzarella cheese, the slices of tomato and some additional oregano and basil on top and heated for an additional minute to melt the cheese. We thought it came out great.

It was good and easy. I substituted a couple of Hot Coppa slices for Ham, added Italian Seasoning and olive oil on the thick loin chops with the salt and pepper. I did add the Coppa, fresh moz, and romas 3/4 of the way through cooking the 2nd side so everything was done and the meat wasn't overcooked.

Really easy to make and easily customizable for your tastebuds. My husband is lactose intolerant so I opted to use Swiss cheese for half of the batch. I used Italian seasonings instead of just the oregano on both sides of the pork chop and I baked it instead (I don't have a grill right now). Salt was only added to the one side after I had laid it on the baking sheet.

So simple yet delicious (even with Swiss cheese instead of mozzarella). It really did only take 10 minutes to prep it.

I made this in the oven. I seared them first. About 2 minutes in each side. Weren't very think. Then I put the tomatoes on the pan just a little to make warm. Place them on the hot chop. Sprinkle cheese. Broiled it. Didn't use ham. In total it was just a few minutes. In the beginning I rinsed the chops, dried them, then seasoned them. Then searing. My partner and I Loved it!
I used thin chops and left out the ham added garlic 100% better than plain pork chops. Served with homemade noodles and Alfredo sauce

I liked it but omitted the ham, I thought the chop was plenty. Bought chips from Costco and cut them in half because they are rather thick. Did like recipe but put in broiler to melt the cheese so the chops did not dry out. Great quick dinner!!

Turned out great! I didn’t have fresh oregano, so I sprinkled some Italian seasoning mix on the pork with some Worcestershire sauce before grilling. Canadian bacon (cause I needed to get rid of it) and shredded mozzarella under the tomato finished it up. Yummy!
Awesome , used fresh mozzarella pearls , fresh basil and cured ham, thinly sliced . Thanks for the recipe !
Sounds good, but cooking the pork to 160 isd to much, pork needs to be cooked till 145 degrees.
Husband who doesn't care for pork loved this !
Followed the recipe exactly and it was DELICIOUS! And, super easy. It was enhanced by the fresh tomatoes and oregano from my garden.
My husband loved it! The tomato added moisture. I added bacon with the ham and used an Italian cheese blend. Great recipe! Will definitely make it again. Nancy H.
They were delicious!! Lots of flavor!!

Really solid! Cant say I followed it to the t. In France so added a french twist to it instead of italien but absolutely loved it. served over pasta made for a hearty meal! Also added basil to give it a little more flare! Thanks for sharing!
Nothing special, but easy. I ex'd the ham and used a balsamic vinegarette glaze, which made it pop as desired.
This really is a great recipe. Loved it.
Came out really juicy, followed recipe, family loved it .
Delicious, and easy
